summary: I audited the range 33488f0..5734bd2. The three test files pass: 18, 13, and 38 cases. The three doc suites pass 51/51, 98/98, and 34/34, and they match the plan. The 8 G20 mutants apply one time, and each mutated source compiles. The old names red_scope and RedScope are gone from the code. I built probes for an unknown track id, an own add-then-delete commit, and a staged-only UX change; each result is correct. Fail-closed behavior holds in each check. No Blocker and no Major exists. I found three Nits: the staged union has no AC case, and two doc sentences are less exact than the code. Task 3.4 (AC-20) is still [~], so the plan makes no false claim.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] tests/spec_review_gate/test_gate_track_scope.py: D5 names the staged diff, but no AC case stages a change; AC-13 covers only the unstaged diff. Rationale: a regression that drops the `--cached` union would keep all 18 cases green; I confirmed the staged branch works with a probe.

F2 [Nit] skills/measure-orchestrator/references/contracts.md (Track scope): the sentence 'When `git log` cannot list the range, the check keeps the full committed-file set' does not state the jr-green HEAD-check fallback. Rationale: jr-green reads no committed-file set; the operator contract is less exact than the code for that D2 failure path.

F3 [Nit] CHANGELOG.md: the sentence 'Each check prints each skipped commit as an `INFO:` line' is not exact. The spec-review gate prints no INFO line when its tree diff fails (AC-6, D4). Rationale: the entry would mislead a reader about that failure path.
